QuestionStmt.S: Which of the following aqueous solutions exhibits lowest freezing point depression assuming complete dissociation?

Solution.S:
Freezing point depression is a colligative property — it depends on the total number of particles (ions) in the solution. Lower the number of particles, lower the depression.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Solution} & \text{Dissociation} & \text{Ion molality} \\
\hline
0.1\ m\ \mathrm{NaCl} & \mathrm{NaCl \rightarrow Na^+ + Cl^-} & 0.1 \times 2 = 0.2\ m \\
0.05\ m\ \mathrm{MgSO_4} & \mathrm{MgSO_4 \rightarrow Mg^{2+} + SO_4^{2-}} & 0.05 \times 2 = 0.1\ m \\
0.08\ m\ \mathrm{AlPO_4} & \mathrm{AlPO_4 \rightarrow Al^{3+} + PO_4^{3-}} & 0.08 \times 2 = 0.16\ m \\
0.06\ m\ \mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3} & \mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3 \rightarrow 2Al^{3+} + 3SO_4^{2-}} & 0.06 \times 5 = 0.3\ m \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

The lowest ion molality is for 0.05 m MgSO₄, hence it will show the lowest freezing point depression.

Therefore, the correct option is B.
